details:
Project Details

Our project is an interactive 3D web experience that transforms the history of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars into an engaging space exploration journey.

Users can explore 3D representations of the Solar System, select the Moon or Mars, and navigate their planetary environments to discover spacecraft and equipment left behind by past and recent missions. The project features 10 lunar artifacts and 9 Martian spacecraft, including Apollo 11's Lunar Module, Apollo 15's Lunar Roving Vehicle, Lunokhod 1, Curiosity, Opportunity, Perseverance, and Ingenuity. Each featured object is presented through its mission story, historical background, images, available 3D models, and landing location.

To develop the experience, we used NASA mission records, scientific resources, images, and available 3D models, alongside selected resources from other space agencies and external providers. These resources help connect each object to its real mission and historical context.

The frontend was developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with Three.js and WebGL for interactive 3D visualization. We used GLB/GLTF assets for planetary environments and spacecraft models, and Python's HTTP server for local development and testing.

The creative aspect of our project is the combination of space history, 3D exploration, and storytelling in one experience. Instead of presenting discarded equipment as a static list or collection of facts, we allow users to discover these objects in the context of the worlds where they were left behind.

During development, we considered historical accuracy, the reliability of information, the availability and quality of 3D assets, the clarity of the user experience, and the distinction between confirmed mission facts and visual representations.

Our intended impact is to make space exploration history more accessible and engaging for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. By revealing the stories behind equipment that remains on other worlds, we aim to encourage curiosity, support space education, and highlight the lasting human footprint beyond Earth.
